title: SQL database in Microsoft Fabric — Overview

claims.text: SQL database in Fabric is a developer-oriented transactional database engine that shares the same underlying SQL Database Engine as Azure SQL Database, making it the designated home for OLTP workloads within the Fabric platform.

When a SQL database is created in Fabric, the platform automatically and continuously replicates its data into OneLake in near-real time, converting it to Parquet format so that downstream analytical services — Spark, notebooks, Power BI, data engineering pipelines — can consume it without any manual export step.

Provisioning a SQL database in a Fabric workspace also automatically creates a companion SQL analytics endpoint, giving read-only analytical access to the replicated OneLake data without affecting the transactional workload.

SQL database in Fabric enables translytical application patterns by separating write traffic (through the transactional engine) from read/analytics traffic (through the SQL analytics endpoint backed by OneLake), eliminating contention between the two workloads.
The database ships with automatic tuning enabled by default, including automatic index creation, so routine index management is handled autonomously rather than requiring manual DBA intervention.

SQL database supports vector data types and integrates with Azure OpenAI and orchestration frameworks such as LangChain and Semantic Kernel, positioning it as a store for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and semantic search workloads inside Fabric.

Because the replicated OneLake data is stored as Delta tables, a SQL analytics endpoint on one database can join data from other Fabric items — warehouses, mirrored databases, or other SQL databases — using standard three-part T-SQL naming, enabling cross-database federated queries without data movement.

Authentication to a SQL database in Fabric is exclusively via Microsoft Entra ID; SQL authentication is not supported. A user, service principal, or group must hold at least the Read item permission on the database in Fabric before any connection succeeds.

Security features include row-level security (RLS), object-level security (OLS), workspace-level customer-managed keys, and SQL auditing, bringing enterprise-grade access control and compliance capabilities to the transactional database inside Fabric.

SQL database in Fabric does not map to Azure SQL elastic pools; instead, a single Fabric capacity spans multiple Fabric SQL databases across different workspaces, consolidating billing and providing resource sharing analogous to elastic pools while maintaining workspace-level security isolation.

For organisations with data already in Azure SQL Database, Fabric Mirroring provides a low-latency, low-cost path to continuously replicate that existing estate into Fabric's OneLake without rebuilding the source database.

Database portability is handled via SqlPackage, which supports .bacpac import/export and .dacpac schema deployments, enabling migration between Azure SQL Database and Fabric SQL database and supporting CI/CD-style incremental schema changes through SQL projects.

Beyond translytical apps, Microsoft now documents two additional named usage patterns for SQL database in Fabric: reverse ETL, where curated analytical output from warehouses or lakehouses is pushed back into the SQL database so applications, APIs, and GraphQL endpoints can consume it operationally; and an operational data store role, consolidating multiple operational systems into one normalized, near-real-time store for lightweight reporting.
The Fabric portal can generate a GraphQL API directly over a SQL database, and the database also integrates with Fabric's built-in git-based source control for CI/CD-style workflows.
